proposals.relationship: Ginzburg disputes Furet’s restriction of subordinate-class history to quantitative and anonymous reconstruction, defending individual cases where the evidence permits.
proposals.evidence_note: He explicitly names Furet before defending the possibility of reconstructing individual personalities. This is a methodological criticism, not rejection of quantitative history as such or proof of every Menocchio interpretation. Furet’s underlying text was not newly read.

proposals.evidence_note: The joint paper recognizes Hall’s sophisticated anti-essentialism; it neither labels him a simple essentialist nor denies the political legitimacy of identity claims.
